doc.interviewee: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant

title: Bunk Johnson's generosity and the home he never bought
summary: Synigal remembers Bunk as a fine, charming player who gave away his money and died before buying a home; the block ends in garbled ASR looping.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Bunk Jones. Bunk Jones was the father of those guys. He comes to music. So many of them, I can't recall right now exactly that band. He played music with Bunk Jones. He was a fine player. A good mixer. He was very charming, too. He was a fellow who gave his heart out to everybody else and leave himself in the morning. He really did that. He used to give away all he made. Way around the last. On the last part, he found out he was getting old. He came to me. He said, you know, Calvary. I said, I don't know. I've done a lot of good work. I've done plenty of money, but I don't have any money. I've done enough. I don't even want a home. I said, well, you don't have any. At that time, my folks were dead. I said, I'd like to sell you by. He was getting prepared to buy the home at that time. He said, you know, I got $4,000. I had to buy it. I said, you know, we sell it to you for four thousand. He went off. Well, my brother, he wouldn't agree to run on the home at that time. He drifted off. He finally died before he got the home. Yeah. Because he lived just about a block from us. He was raised up from us. Just about a block from us. They were all raised up together. We all went to school together. He went to school with us. We went on and on and on. He spent all his time in music. All his time in Spanish music. He looked at half and half days. He left to build for dear
